reader.requirement: An EXIT PROGRAM executed in a called program with the INITIAL attribute also performs the CANCEL of that program: its open internal files are implicitly closed without USE procedures (EXTERNAL connectors stay open), every program it contains is cancelled (their files closed, their storage reset), and the program is at present cancelled.

The INITIAL clause is admitted at 85 (the probe compiled).

reader.notes: EXIT PROGRAM emits a ProgramReturn under __asCalled; CallProgram's finally runs EndInitialActivation for an INITIAL node on return, which runs the emitted CloseFiles (internal, non-SD files, no USE hook), cancels contained programs in reverse order through CancelNode and marks the program cancelled. The path never consults the edition.

refuter.evidence: Probes at --std 85: x_nest_init.cob (run x_nest_init-001): a NESTED program XNI IS INITIAL inside a non-initial container opens its own file LF1 and writes the container's GLOBAL file GF; after its EXIT PROGRAM, LS1 (moved to 99 just before the EXIT) reads 00 (the implicit CLOSE stored its status), the re-CALL's OPEN of LF1 gives 00 not 41, N restarts at 1, and the container's GLOBAL GF stays open (its WRITE after each return gives 00). x_main_init.cob (run x_main_init-001): a main program with IS INITIAL, not under a caller, executing EXIT PROGRAM continues with the next statement (GR1): CNT stays 5 and its file stays open (WRITE and CLOSE give 00), so no CANCEL is applied there. cite.py: OK §1985:X.5.4.4 GR3 the text is in GR3; OK §1985:X.5.4.4 GR1 the text is in GR1. The reader's x_init covered contained-program cancel and an EXTERNAL file.
